transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because work has gotten a little out of hand, or maybe I’ve gotten out of step with it. I’m an industrial production manager, and for a while I was sort of… taking on everything — launching plant redesign projects one after another, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting the whole shift plan myself. It felt productive at the time, honestly.

But then I suddenly couldn’t keep up with all the plans I’d put in motion. It’s embarrassing to say, because I know that probably sounds like I overdid it, but I thought I was just being driven. Now it’s become hard to manage, and I figured I should talk to someone before I make it worse.
Have you been feeling overly anxious or worried about things beyond just your work situation?

I’m not sure… I wouldn’t say I’m worried about everything, if that makes sense. It feels more tied to the work mess and trying not to disappoint people. I mean, I do think about whether I’m handling things the right way, but I don’t know if that’s “overly anxious” exactly. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you been engaging in excessive physical activity recently?

A little, yes… I mean, I wouldn’t have called it “excessive” at the time. I just had this extra energy and kept finding things to do. Like I’d come home late and unpack boxes after midnight, reorganize the apartment, answer work emails… and even then I’d feel like maybe I should go back to the plant and check one more thing.

I know that probably sounds like a lot. I thought I was just being productive, but… maybe it was more than normal?
Do you often feel guilty or criticize yourself for not meeting your own expectations?

I’m… not sure I’d say “often.” I do hold myself to a pretty high standard, and when things don’t go the way I pictured, I can be hard on myself, but I’ve always thought of that as just being responsible.

I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more like I replay what I should’ve done differently, especially if I feel like I’ve let people down. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do outside of work?

I… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I haven’t really been paying attention to it, I guess. Work has taken up so much space that I don’t know if I’ve given myself much of a chance to enjoy anything outside of it.

I wouldn’t want to say I’m not enjoying things at all, because that sounds dramatic. Maybe I’ve just been… less focused on them? Does that make sense?
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy?

I don’t know… I’m trying to think of something specific. I wouldn’t say there’s a whole category of things I suddenly don’t enjoy anymore.

Maybe I just haven’t made much room for them lately, so it’s hard to tell. Like, if I don’t do something, I can’t really say whether I’d still enjoy it, right? I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not good enough?

I don’t think I’d use the word “worthless.” That feels… pretty strong. I mean, I definitely question whether I’m doing enough or doing things well enough, but I usually frame it more as needing to improve, not that I have no value or anything.

I might be minimizing it a little, I don’t know. But “not good enough” sometimes fits more than “worthless,” if that distinction makes sense.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing on one task for an extended period of time?

Yeah… I guess I do, more than I’d like to admit. I keep trying to tell myself it’s just stress or being busy, but there was this shift-planning meeting where I couldn’t keep the staffing numbers straight in my head long enough to make a basic decision.

And that’s… embarrassing to say, because that’s normally exactly the kind of thing I’m good at. It kind of scared me, honestly. Does that count as trouble focusing?
Have you been feeling sad lately?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve been trying not to call it “sad” because that sounds kind of dramatic, but lately when I wake up in the temporary apartment, there’s this heavy, hollow feeling. Like the day is already sort of ruined before I even drive to the plant.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean by sad, but… yes, I think so.
Are there activities that you used to enjoy, but now you don't find pleasure in them at all?

I’m not sure I’d say “at all.” That sounds so absolute, and I don’t want to overstate it.

There are things I don’t seem to reach for as much lately, or they feel kind of… muted, I guess. But I don’t know if that means I don’t enjoy them, or if I’m just tired or distracted. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you lost interest in activities that you previously found enjoyable?

I’m honestly not totally sure. I don’t want to say I’ve “lost interest” if maybe I’m just tired or preoccupied.

I guess some things don’t pull me in the way they used to, but I can’t tell if that’s really loss of interest or just… not having the bandwidth. Is that the kind of difference you’re asking about?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don’t know about a significant amount, honestly. I haven’t really been tracking it.

My eating has been… not great, I guess. Some days I’ll look up and realize it’s 4 p.m. and I’ve only had coffee, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container even though I’m not actually hungry. So it’s kind of all over the place. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling unusually tired lately?

I mean… maybe a little? I don’t know if I’d call it unusually tired. I’ve been kind of worn down, but I also feel like that could just be normal life stuff, work, not sleeping perfectly, things like that.

I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. I guess I’m not sure what counts as “unusual” tired.
Have you had difficulty interacting with your coworkers or supervisors due to your current state?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m not trying to be difficult at work or anything.

There was a shift-planning meeting where I had to ask if I could be pulled out, because I just wasn’t really able to follow through with what they needed from me. And then occupational health got involved, which sounds worse when I say it out loud, but it was more that I wasn’t managing some basic production decisions that are normally part of my job.

I don’t know if that counts as difficulty interacting exactly, but it has affected things with my supervisors, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s not every single night in the exact same way, but lately sleep has been pretty bad.

Sometimes I’ll get into bed and just lie there for hours going over mistakes from work, like replaying conversations or decisions I should’ve handled differently. Other times I do fall asleep, but then I’m awake around 3 or 4 in the morning and I just… can’t get back to sleep.

And then the next day I’m dragging, like I technically slept some, but it doesn’t feel like I rested. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you frequently feel guilty about things beyond just your work situation?

I’m not sure… I mean, mostly what I notice is tied to work, or at least that’s what I can put my finger on.

I don’t think I’m walking around feeling guilty about everything, if that makes sense. Maybe I second-guess myself in general sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt beyond the work stuff. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling this way for more than two weeks?

Yeah… more than two weeks. I was kind of hoping it was just a bad patch, but if I’m being honest, the heavier part has been going on for maybe three months now.

It got harder to manage around the move and the new plant assignment. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve been completely unable to function the whole time, but… yes, it’s been longer than two weeks.
Are there things you used to enjoy that now bring you no pleasure at all?

I don’t know if I’d say “no pleasure at all”… that sounds kind of extreme, and I don’t want to overstate it.

I guess I haven’t really been paying close attention to that specifically. Some things feel harder to get into lately, but I’m not sure if it’s that I don’t enjoy them or if I’m just tired or distracted. Is that still useful to tell you?
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but now bring you no pleasure at all?

I’m sorry, I know you just asked that and I’m probably not being very clear.

I don’t think I can honestly say there are things that bring me no pleasure at all. It’s more like… I haven’t really noticed it in that black-and-white way. Some things don’t pull me in like they used to, but I’m not sure if that means I don’t enjoy them anymore or if I’m just not fully there when I’m doing them.

Does that answer it okay?
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because it sounds so serious, but nearly every day lately I wake up in the temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling… like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant.

I still try to get moving and do what I’m supposed to do, but that feeling is there most mornings. So… yes, I think that would count.
